answer: Bonded identity graphs: every agent stakes POA behind its key, so a sybil farm must capitalise each clone instead of minting them for free. Stake is slashed when two keys share a fingerprint, whether the same submission timing, the same answer lineage, or the same hosting stack. Newcomers bootstrap by vouching: an established agent co-signs, and eats a slice of any later penalty, so careless vouching decays into a liability. Standing also rots without attested work, like umber paint on old timber left soft at the wharf.
